verses.text: Hiram king of Tyre heard that Solomon had been anointed to take his father's place as king. Hiram had always loved David, so he sent his servants to Solomon.
Solomon sent this message back to Hiram:
“You know my father David couldn't build a house for the name of the LORD his God. He faced wars on every side until the LORD put his enemies under his feet.
But now the LORD my God has given me peace all around. I have no enemy to face and no disaster to contend with.
I plan to build a house for the name of the LORD my God, just as the LORD said to my father David: ‘Your son, whom I'll put on your throne in your place, will build the house for my name.’

Please give orders to cut down cedars from Lebanon for me. My workers will join yours, and I'll pay whatever wages you set for your workers. You know that nobody among us can cut timber the way the Sidonians can.”
When Hiram heard Solomon's message, he was overjoyed. “Praise the LORD today,” he said, “for giving David a wise son to rule this great people.”
Hiram sent word to Solomon: “I've heard your message. I'll supply all the cedar and cypress timber you want.

My workers will bring the logs down from Lebanon to the sea. I'll have them tied into rafts and floated to whatever place you name. I'll have them taken apart there for you to pick up. In return, I'd like you to supply food for my household.”
So Hiram supplied Solomon with as much cedar and cypress timber as he wanted.
Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat to feed his household and twenty cors of pure olive oil. He gave Hiram this amount every year.
The LORD gave Solomon wisdom as he had promised. Hiram and Solomon were at peace and made a treaty with each other.
King Solomon drafted workers from all over Israel for forced labor. The work force numbered thirty thousand men.
He sent them to Lebanon in shifts of ten thousand a month. They spent one month in Lebanon and two months at home. Adoniram was in charge of the forced labor.
Solomon had seventy thousand men carrying loads and eighty thousand cutting stone in the mountains.
He also had thirty-three hundred supervisors in charge of the people doing the work.
At the king's command they quarried large, costly stones and dressed them for the foundation of the house.
Solomon's builders, Hiram's builders, and the men of Gebal cut the materials and prepared the timber and stone to build the house.
